program_name: Consumer Rights Act 2015 (Statutory Rights on Goods)
jurisdiction: England, Wales, and Northern Ireland (5 years in Scotland)
core_standard: Goods must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose, and as described
mandatory_conditions: Claim is made against the selling retailer, not the manufacturer
Proof of purchase from the specific retailer must be provided
Failure must relate to lack of satisfactory quality or inherent defect
exclusions_and_caveats: Important: This is a legal limitation period to bring a claim, NOT a 6-year warranty
Because the fault occurred after the first 6 months, the customer can be asked to prove the item was faulty when purchased (burden of proof shifts to consumer)
Remedy is subject to proportionality: repair or replacement first; partial refund may account for consumer's period of trouble-free use
